findings.title: Revalidate lead authority when admitting the protected-ref effect

requirement.quote: Mutating commands authenticate a scoped principal and check expected revision/current authority.

findings.behavior: A lead land request is authenticated and generically journaled in dispatch. land_candidate checks accepted/current candidate, drops the database lock for evidence/import/head, then creates the actionable protected-ref intent without any Principal or epoch check. replace_lead can complete in that interval because it does not take git_effect_gate. The superseded lead request still reaches CAS; dispatch reauthentication only rejects the response after confirm_landing has changed the ref and task.
findings.repair: Carry actor identity into land admission; atomically validate current authority and exact candidate/proof while committing the fully authorized immutable broker effect intent. A correctly admitted effect may survive later lead replacement. Add a public barrier control proving replacement before this admission prevents the ref effect, while replacement after it permits properly journaled recovery.
findings.basis: Static control-flow inference; not executed by reviewer.

findings.title: Publish recovered landing disposition exactly once

requirement.quote: Controller publishes progress and disposition through idempotent journaled synchronization.

findings.behavior: At the tested after_ref_update crash point, startup recover calls confirm_landing, updates project base/task to landed and confirms the operation. It does not increment project revision, append a landing event, enqueue a Kata effect, or retain the command receipt. These actions occur only in normal dispatch. With the worker already exited and no original-client retry, event consumers and Kata remain at the prior disposition indefinitely; confirmed operations are no longer recovered. The existing crash oracle checks SQLite/ref identity, not publication.
findings.repair: Make confirmation and recovered disposition publication one idempotent durable transition, or retain a publication-pending operation that recovery drains independent of the old client grant. Prove after-ref-update restart with no client retry produces one landing event/revision and one retryable Kata disposition, including lead replacement.
findings.basis: Static control-flow inference supported by existing crash fixture source; not executed by reviewer.

findings.title: Prevent a live worker grant from reopening a landed task

requirement.quote: Attempt grants permit own brief, messages, progress and submission, not acceptance or landing.

findings.behavior: Landing leaves the attempt running and its submission epoch intact. A subsequent capture_candidate using the same grant, even with the same commit, passes the task guard because only aborted is excluded. It replaces current_candidate and writes state=submitted over landed, superseding the candidate referenced by the authorized acceptance while the protected ref remains landed. The normal fixture itself lands before stopping its worker, so this requires no timing race. Repeating accept_candidate on a landed candidate similarly writes accepted.
findings.repair: Enforce task lifecycle preconditions under the publication transaction so landed tasks cannot be reopened by capture/accept/repeated stale land commands. Preserve immutable prior evidence and require an explicitly authorized new task/rework transition for further work. Add a public post-landing live-worker submission refusal and ensure task/ref/current-candidate remain unchanged.
findings.basis: Static transition inference; not executed by reviewer.
